$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{3}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{3}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=6x+1$ for $x\in [-3,3).$ The Fourier series of the $6$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${b}_{5}.$

${b}_{5}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the sine coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=3$ and $f(x)=6x+1$ for $x\in (-3,3).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{b}_{5}=\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-3}^{3}(6x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x+1\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}x)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{3}{5\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}x)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{5} & =\frac{1}{3}(uv\,{|}_{-3}^{3}-{\int }_{-3}^{3}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(-\frac{3}{5\pi }{[(6x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}x)]}_{-3}^{3}+\frac{18}{5\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{5\pi }(-{[(6x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}x)]}_{-3}^{3}+6{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{5\pi }(-((6(3)+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\pi )-(6(-3)+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(-5\pi ))+\frac{18}{5\pi }{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}x)]}_{-3}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5\pi }(36+\frac{18}{5\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-5\pi ))) \\  & =\frac{1}{5\pi }\cdot 36 \\  & =\frac{36}{5\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Let $F(x)=4{x}^{2}-6x+3$ for $x\in [-3,3).$ The Fourier series of the $6$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=3$ and $f(x)=4{x}^{2}-6x+3$ for $x\in [-3,3).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-3}^{3}(4{x}^{2}-6x+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+3x]}_{-3}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}((\frac{4}{3}\cdot {3}^{3}-3\cdot {3}^{2}+3\cdot 3)-(\frac{4}{3}\cdot (-3)^{3}-3\cdot (-3)^{2}+3\cdot (-3))) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(18-(-72)) \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$

f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=3{x}^{2}+4x$ for $x\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}).$ The Fourier series of the $\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $f(x)=3{x}^{2}+4x$ for $x\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(3{x}^{2}+4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}]}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }((\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{8}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2})-(-\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{8}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2})) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{4}) \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Let $F(x)=3x+\frac{1}{2}$ for $x\in [-9,9).$ The Fourier series of the $18$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=9$ and $f(x)=3x+\frac{1}{2}$ for $x\in [-9,9).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{9}{\int }_{-9}^{9}(3x+\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}x]}_{-9}^{9} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}((\frac{3}{2}\cdot {9}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 9)-(\frac{3}{2}\cdot (-9)^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-9))) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(126-117) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{3}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{3}x)
$$

The Fourier series of the $6$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1, & x\in [0,3) \\ -4, & x\in [-3,0)\end{aligned}
$$

is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{2}.$

${a}_{2}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the cosine coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=3.$ Also, $f(x)=1$ for $x\in [0,3)$ and $f(x)=-4$ for $x\in [-3,0).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-3}^{0}(-4)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}x)\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2\pi }{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}x)]}_{-3}^{0}+\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2\pi }{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}x)]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2\pi ))+\frac{1}{2\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
